mainTopic: Who and what comes first: the order of קרבנות, of people in rescue and honor, and of lineage, where Torah learning outranks every status.
overview: The amud is all about who or what comes first. It starts with קרבנות. The כהן משיח's bull comes before the community's bull, and every חטאת comes before an עולה. The one exception is the bull and goat for עבודה זרה, explained by the missing א in לחטת or by the word כמשפט. A ברייתא then ranks more offerings: communal before individual, king before commoner, female goat against ewe (a disagreement of תנאים), and the עומר and שתי הלחם before their sheep. A new משנה turns to people: when a man comes first and when a woman comes first for rescue, clothing and captivity. The גמרא ranks a person, his teacher and his parents, then חכם, מלך, כהן גדול, נביא, and all the levels of כהנים and Temple officials. It also explains why the סגן, not the משוח מלחמה, stays טהור. A final משנה ranks people by lineage, from כהן down to freed slave, but a learned ממזר comes before an ignorant כהן גדול, because Torah is 'more precious than pearls.' The amud closes with questions students asked about converts, freed maidservants, cats and mice.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה and asking for its source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the כהן משיח's bull comes before the community's bull, and asks where this comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the bull of the anointed כהן and the bull of the community, etc. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a line from the משנה and asks for its source in the תורה. This sets up the next step, which will give the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the כהן משיח's bull comes first 'in all its actions,' but it did not give a reason. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this order.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull the anointed כהן גדול brings when he rules wrongly and acts on his ruling
The bull the whole community brings when it follows a mistaken ruling of the בית דין
From where are these words learned? (asking for a source)

phrases.aramaic: פַּר כֹּהֵן מָשׁוּחַ וּפַר עֵדָה כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: The bull of the anointed priest and the bull of the congregation, etc.
phrases.notes: 'כו׳' means 'and so on.' The גמרא quotes only the start of the משנה's line, which ends that the כהן's bull comes first.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the משנה's line.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the כהן משיח's bull coming before the community's bull.

steps.title: The word 'the first' teaches the priest's bull comes first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the extra word 'הראשון' that the כהן משיח's bull comes before the community's bull in everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'And he shall burn it as he burned the first bull.' Why does the פסוק need to say 'the first'? To teach that the first one comes before the community's bull in all its actions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא reads an extra word in the פסוק as a source for the order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the community's bull compares its burning to 'the first bull,' meaning the כהן משיח's bull from the section before. The word 'הראשון' seems unneeded, since the פסוק could just say 'the bull.' So the ברייתא reads 'first' as a rule: that bull is first in order, every time.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק come to teach? (pointing out a word that seems extra)
In all its actions (slaughtering, sprinkling, burning, and so on)

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"And he shall burn it as he burned
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:21

phrases.english: the first bull";
why must the verse state "the first"?
So that it will be first,
preceding the bull of the congregation in all its actions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'הראשון' teaches that the כהן משיח's bull is first in all its actions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method: a word that seems extra in a פסוק is read as teaching a new rule.

steps.title: A ברייתא states the priest's bull goes first
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא repeats the rule that when both bulls are waiting, the כהן משיח's bull goes first in everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if the bull of the anointed כהן and the bull of the community are both waiting, the anointed כהן's bull comes before the community's bull in all its actions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that states the same ruling. This sets up the next step, where this ברייתא gives a logical reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is both bulls ready to be offered at the same time. The ruling matches the משנה. What is new in this ברייתא is the reason that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing, meaning both are waiting to be offered

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: פַּר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ וּפַר הָעֵדָה עוֹמְדִים –
phrases.english: If the bull of the anointed priest and the bull of the congregation are pending,

phrases.aramaic: פַּר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ קוֹדֵם לְפַר הָעֵדָה
phrases.english: the bull of the anointed priest precedes the bull of the congregation
in all its actions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא with the same rule, which will give a different kind of support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both bulls are waiting, the כהן משיח's bull goes first in every stage.

steps.title: The one who atones goes before those he atones for
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the כהן atones and the community receives atonement, so the כהן goes first, as the פסוק about יום כיפור shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the anointed כהן brings atonement and the community receives atonement, it makes sense that the one who brings atonement should go before the one receiving it. And so the פסוק says: 'And he shall atone for himself, and for his household, and for all the congregation of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a logical reason for the rule and then backs it up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is that the כהן is the one who does the atoning for the people, so his own atonement should come first. The פסוק about the כהן גדול on יום כיפור shows the same order: first himself, then his family, then all ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical / it makes sense
And so the פסוק says (bringing support)

phrases.english: Since the anointed priest atones,
and the congregation gains atonement,
it is logical that the one who atones should precede the one who gains atonement,
and so it says:
"And he shall atone for himself, and for his household,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:17

phrases.english: and for all the congregation of Israel."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason and a supporting פסוק for the rule in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the כהן משיח's bull precedes the community's bull.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic (the one who atones comes first) and ויקרא 16:17, where the כהן atones for himself before all ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: The כהן משיח's bull comes first for two reasons: the word 'הראשון,' and the logic that the one who atones goes before those he atones for.

steps.title: The bull for a communal mistake comes before the bull for idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the community's bull for an ordinary mistaken ruling comes before the community's bull for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bull brought for a matter hidden from the community comes before the bull brought for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states a new rule of order between two communal bulls. This sets up the גמרא's question about why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both bulls are brought by the community. One is for an ordinary mistaken ruling (העלם דבר), and the other is for a mistake about עבודה זרה. The ברייתא says the ordinary one goes first.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter hidden from the community: when the בית דין rules wrongly and the people act on it

phrases.english: The bull for an unwitting communal sin
precedes the bull for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר קוֹדֵם לְפַר שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new comparison of order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bull for an ordinary communal mistake comes before the bull for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Asking for the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ordinary communal bull comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule in step 5. It is setting up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are bulls brought by the community, so it is not clear why one should go first. The גמרא wants a principle that explains it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the bull for an ordinary communal mistake precedes the bull for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: One is a חטאת and the other an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ordinary communal bull is a חטאת, while the bull for עבודה זרה is an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is a חטאת and that one is an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two bulls are different kinds of offerings. Next it will bring a source that a חטאת comes before an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bull for an ordinary communal mistake is a חטאת. The bull for עבודה זרה is an עולה, as the פסוק in במדבר says. So the question becomes a general one: which type of offering goes first?

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt-offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: This is a sin-offering and that is a burnt-offering,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the bull for the ordinary mistake, and 'that' is the bull for עבודה זרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by naming the type of each offering.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first bull is a חטאת and the second is an עולה, and a חטאת comes first.

steps.title: A בנה אב that every חטאת comes before its עולה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that 'first' in the פסוק about bird offerings is not needed for that case. So it teaches a general rule that every חטאת comes before the עולה brought with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: 'And he shall offer the one for a חטאת first.' Why does the פסוק say this? If it is to teach that the חטאת comes first, it already says: 'And the second he shall make an עולה, according to the law.' Rather, this sets up a model: every חטאת comes before the עולות brought with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof that a חטאת always goes before an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a pair of birds, the פסוק already shows the חטאת comes first, because it calls the עולה 'the second.' So the word 'first' is extra. The ברייתא uses that extra word as a בנה אב: a general rule for all offerings, which covers the bulls in our case.

keyTerms.meaning: But it already says (showing a word is not needed for this point)
Built a model: a source that sets a general rule for all similar cases

phrases.english: And it is taught:
"And he shall sacrifice that which is for the sin-offering first";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:8

phrases.english: why must the verse state this?
If it is to teach that the sin-offering will be first,
it is already stated:
"And the second he shall prepare as a burnt-offering according to the ordinance"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:10

phrases.english: Rather, this established a paradigm
that all sin-offerings precede
the burnt-offerings that come with them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the principle that the answer in step 7 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That a חטאת comes before an עולה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra word 'ראשונה' in ויקרא 5:8, which is not needed since ויקרא 5:10 already calls the עולה 'the second.'
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is about a pair of birds, but the rule learned from it covers all offerings, including our communal bulls.

steps.title: Even a bird sin-offering beats an animal burnt-offering
steps.stepSummary: The rule is strong enough that even a bird חטאת comes before an animal עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we hold that even a bird חטאת comes before an animal עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds how far the rule reaches: the type of offering decides the order, not how big or costly the animal is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a larger animal offering should come first. The גמרא says no: being a חטאת is what gives the priority, even when the חטאת is only a bird.

phrases.english: and we maintain that even bird sin-offerings
precede animal burnt-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule from step 8 to its widest case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A חטאת always goes before an עולה, even a bird חטאת before an animal עולה.
steps.whatToRemember: A חטאת comes before an עולה. This is learned as a בנה אב from 'ראשונה' and holds even for a bird חטאת against an animal עולה. That is why the ordinary communal bull (a חטאת) beats the bull for עבודה זרה (an עולה).

steps.title: The bull for idol worship comes before the goat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that the community's bull for עבודה זרה is offered before its goat for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bull for עבודה זרה comes before the goat for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states one more rule of order. This sets up a challenge, because it seems to clash with the rule just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a communal mistake about עבודה זרה, the community brings a bull and a goat. The ברייתא says the bull goes first.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat the community brings for a mistake about עבודה זרה

phrases.english: A bull for idol worship precedes
a goat for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה קוֹדֵם לִשְׂעִיר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a new ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bull for עבודה זרה is offered before the goat for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: But the goat is a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling: the goat is a חטאת and the bull is an עולה, so the goat should come first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? This one is a חטאת and that one is an עולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling in step 10 using the rule it just proved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that every חטאת comes before an עולה. With עבודה זרה, the goat is the חטאת and the bull is the עולה. So by that rule the goat should go first, which is the opposite of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Why?
This is a sin-offering, and that is a burnt-offering!
phrases.notes: Now 'this' is the goat (a חטאת) and 'that' is the bull (an עולה).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10 using the rule from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the bull for עבודה זרה precedes the goat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every חטאת comes before an עולה. The goat is a חטאת and the bull is an עולה, so the goat should come first.

steps.title: The missing א in the word for sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they answered, in the name of רבא בר מרי, that the word for this חטאת is written without an א, which shows it does not get the full status of a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they say in the name of רבא בר מרי: the חטאת of עבודה זרה is missing an א, since 'לחטת' is what is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer to the challenge, based on how a word in the פסוק is spelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק about the bull and goat for עבודה זרה, the word for חטאת is spelled without an א. The missing letter shows that this goat is a lesser חטאת. It does not get every rule of a חטאת, including going first. This is still a case of a חטאת; it is just an exception to the usual order.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: They say in the West
in the name of Rava bar Mari:
The sin-offering of idol worship is lacking an alef;
"leḥattat" is written.
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:24. The usual spelling is לחטאת, but here it is written without the א.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא בַּר מָרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception learned from spelling: this חטאת is treated as lesser.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every חטאת, including the goat for עבודה זרה, should come before an עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The missing א shows this goat does not get the priority of a full חטאת, so the bull comes first.

steps.title: רבא: 'according to the law' sets the order
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers differently: the פסוק says 'כמשפט,' meaning the offerings must follow the order written there, bull first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: 'According to the law' is written about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not use the spelling. Instead, he points to the word 'כמשפט' in the same פסוק. He reads it as an instruction to follow the order the פסוק lists, and the פסוק mentions the bull before the goat. So this specific פסוק overrides the general rule that a חטאת goes first.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the law: here read as 'in the set order'

phrases.english: Rava said:
"According to the ordinance" is written concerning it.
phrases.notes: Also in במדבר 15:24, which lists the bull before the goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the challenge of step 11, instead of the answer in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception from an explicit word in the פסוק that fixes the order.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general rule that a חטאת comes first should apply here too.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כמשפט' requires following the order in the פסוק, so the bull comes before the goat.
steps.whatToRemember: For עבודה זרה, the bull (an עולה) comes before the goat (a חטאת). This is an exception to the usual rule. It is explained either by the missing א in 'לחטת' or by the word 'כמשפט.'

steps.title: The community's goat comes before the king's goat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that the community's שעיר for עבודה זרה is offered before the king's goat, because the community comes before an individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: The goat for idol worship comes before the king's goat. Why? This one belongs to the community and that one belongs to one person.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of which קרבן comes first. It puts the community's goat for עבודה זרה ahead of the goat a king brings for his sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both goats are חטאות, so being a חטאת cannot decide the order. The deciding factor is who brings it. A קרבן of the whole צבור comes before a קרבן of a יחיד, even when that יחיד is the king.

phrases.aramaic: שְׂעִיר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה קוֹדֵם לִשְׂעִיר נָשִׂיא.
phrases.english: The goat for idol worship comes before the king's goat.
What is the reason?
This one belongs to the community, and that one belongs to an individual.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׂעִיר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה קוֹדֵם לִשְׂעִיר נָשִׂיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about the bull and goat (steps 11-13), the ברייתא's list of precedence continues.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A communal חטאת goat comes before the king's חטאת goat, because צבור comes before יחיד.

steps.title: The king's goat comes before a regular person's female goat
steps.stepSummary: The king's male goat comes before a regular person's female goat, because a king outranks a commoner.
steps.simpleTranslation: The king's goat comes before a regular person's female goat. Why? This one belongs to a king and that one belongs to a commoner.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves one step down the ladder. The king's goat is placed before the female goat that an ordinary person brings as a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again both are חטאות, so the order depends on the person who brings it. A מלך outranks a הדיוט, so his קרבן is offered first.

keyTerms.meaning: A female goat, the usual חטאת of an ordinary person

phrases.english: The king's goat comes before an individual's female goat.
What is the reason?
This one belongs to a king, and that one belongs to a commoner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list, one level lower.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king's חטאת comes before a commoner's חטאת.

steps.title: A regular person's female goat comes before a regular person's ewe
steps.stepSummary: Between two ordinary people's חטאות, the female goat comes before the ewe (female sheep).
steps.simpleTranslation: An individual's female goat comes before an individual's ewe.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא compares two חטאות brought by ordinary people: one a female goat and one a female sheep. It says the goat comes first. This ruling sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the person bringing each קרבן has the same rank, and both are חטאות. So the order must depend on the type of animal. The ברייתא gives no reason here.

phrases.english: An individual's female goat comes before an individual's ewe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list down to two ordinary people's חטאות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual's female goat חטאת comes before an individual's ewe חטאת.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the ewe comes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a different ברייתא that says the opposite: the ewe comes before the female goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: an individual's ewe comes before an individual's female goat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling it just quoted by bringing another ברייתא that says the exact opposite order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources about the very same case contradict each other. The question is how both can be correct.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: But it was taught in a ברייתא:
An individual's ewe comes before an individual's female goat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 16 with a contradicting source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the female goat comes before the ewe.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא states the reverse order for the same case, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: אביי: Two תנאים disagree, each with a reason
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the two ברייתות reflect a disagreement between תנאים. One holds the goat is more important because it is required for עבודה זרה, and the other holds the ewe is more important because its tail goes on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a disagreement of תנאים. One master holds the female goat is better, since it has an extra use: it is brought for an individual's עבודה זרה. The other master holds the ewe is better, since it has something extra: its fat tail.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות simply follow two different תנאים who disagree. He then gives each side's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side points to a different way its animal is "more." The goat is the only animal allowed when an individual brings a חטאת for עבודה זרה. The ewe has more parts placed on the מזבח, because a sheep's fat tail is also offered.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a disagreement between תנאים
The fat tail of a sheep

steps.whatToRemember: The order between a female goat and a ewe is a disagreement of תנאים: one side points to the goat's special role for עבודה זרה, the other to the ewe's extra fat tail.

phrases.english: אביי said: It is a disagreement between תנאים.
One master holds that a female goat is better,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבְּתָה אֵצֶל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּיָחִיד.
phrases.english: since it has an extra use: it is brought for idol worship by an individual.
phrases.notes: An individual who sins with עבודה זרה must bring a female goat. A ewe is not allowed (במדבר 15:27).

phrases.english: And the other master holds that a ewe is better,
since it has something extra: its fat tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement of תנאים: each ברייתא follows a different opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to be one teaching that contradicts itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are two opinions, each with a reason for why its animal is more important.

steps.title: The עומר and שתי הלחם come before their sheep
steps.stepSummary: The עומר comes before the lamb brought with it, and the שתי הלחם come before the sheep brought with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The עומר comes before the lamb that comes with it. The two loaves come before the sheep that come with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא turns to two special flour offerings that come with animals. It says the flour offering is brought before its accompanying animals. The next step gives the general rule behind this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an animal קרבן seems more important than a flour offering. Here the flour offering comes first anyway, which needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות

phrases.english: The עומר comes before the lamb that comes with it;
the two loaves come before
the sheep that come with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the contradiction, the ברייתא continues its list with a new pair of cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עומר and the שתי הלחם are offered before the animals that come with them.

steps.title: The rule: what the day requires comes before what the bread requires
steps.stepSummary: The general principle is that an offering brought because of the day comes before an offering brought because of the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: something brought because of the day comes before something brought because of the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sums up the last cases with a general rule that explains why the flour offering comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר and שתי הלחם are required because of the day itself. The sheep are brought only because of those flour offerings. What causes the obligation comes before what follows from it.
steps.whatToRemember: The cause comes before the add-on. The day requires the flour offering, and the flour offering brings along the sheep, so the flour offering is first.

phrases.english: This is the rule:
something that comes because of the day
phrases.notes: Some versions have the letters in round brackets and some don't. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: comes before something that comes because of the bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the general principle behind the cases in step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An offering obligated by the day comes before an offering that only accompanies it.

steps.title: New משנה: when a man comes first and when a woman comes first
steps.stepSummary: The משנה moves from קרבנות to people. A man comes first for saving his life and returning a lost item. A woman comes first for clothing and for being freed from captivity.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The man comes before the woman for saving life and returning a lost item. The woman comes before the man for clothing and for freeing from captivity.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It shifts from ordering קרבנות to ordering people, starting with a man versus a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on the kind of help being given. For saving a life and returning a lost item, the man is first. For clothing and freeing from captivity, the woman is first. The משנה does not give the reasons here.
steps.confusionAlert: There is no single "who is more important" rule here. The order changes depending on what kind of help is needed.

phrases.english: משנה:
The man comes before the woman
to save his life and to return a lost item.
And the woman comes before the man
to be given clothing and to be freed from captivity.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִישׁ קוֹדֵם לָאִשָּׁה לְהַחֲיוֹת וּלְהָשֵׁב אֲבֵדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The theme of precedence moves from קרבנות to people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man comes first for saving life and returning a lost item. A woman comes first for clothing and for release from captivity.

steps.title: When both face degradation, the man is freed first
steps.stepSummary: If both the man and the woman are in danger of being degraded in captivity, the man is freed first.
steps.simpleTranslation: When both of them face degradation, the man comes before the woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an exception to its captivity rule. If the man also faces degradation, the normal order flips back and he is freed first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman was put first for captivity because of the risk of degradation she faces. When the man faces the same risk, that difference disappears. The basic order, with the man first, returns.
steps.whatToRemember: The woman goes first in captivity only because of her special danger. When the man faces the same danger, he goes first.

phrases.english: When both of them face degradation,
phrases.notes: He means when the man is also in danger of being abused by the captors, not only the woman.

phrases.english: the man comes before the woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the captivity ruling of step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both captives face degradation, the man is freed before the woman.

steps.title: Who is ransomed first: oneself, one's teacher, one's father, one's mother
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a person's own release comes before his teacher's, his teacher's comes before his father's, and his mother's comes before everyone's.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If a person, his father, and his teacher were all in captivity, he comes before his teacher, and his teacher comes before his father. His mother comes before all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by bringing a ברייתא that adds more cases of who gets ransomed first from captivity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ended with rules about freeing captives, and this ברייתא continues that theme. It gives a clear order: yourself first, then your רבי, then your father. Your mother is placed ahead of all of them.
steps.confusionAlert: 'All of them' clearly includes the father and the teacher. The ברייתא does not spell out whether it also includes the person himself, so be careful not to read more into it than the text says.

phrases.english: Gemara
The Sages taught:
If he, his father, and his teacher were in captivity
he comes before his teacher,
and his teacher comes before his father.
His mother comes before all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה הוּא וְאָבִיו וְרַבּוֹ בַּשֶּׁבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rules about freeing captives with a ברייתא that adds family and teacher cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Self before teacher, teacher before father, and mother before all.

steps.title: A חכם comes before the מלך
steps.stepSummary: A חכם takes priority over a מלך ישראל, because a lost חכם cannot be replaced, while anyone in Israel could become king.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Torah scholar comes before the king of Israel. If a scholar dies, we have no one like him. If a king of Israel dies, all of Israel are fit to be king.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now ranks the great leaders of Israel, starting with the חכם over the מלך, and gives a reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is about who can be replaced. A חכם's Torah knowledge is one of a kind and is lost when he dies. A king can be replaced by anyone fit to rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone like him, an equal replacement

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that Torah greatness ranks above political power.

phrases.english: A Torah scholar comes before the king of Israel:
a scholar who dies,
we have no one like him.
A king of Israel who dies,
all of Israel are fit for kingship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same ברייתא moves from family priority to the ranking of leaders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חכם takes priority over a מלך because he cannot be replaced.

steps.title: The מלך comes before the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: A מלך comes before a כהן גדול, proven from a פסוק where King דוד speaks to צדוק the כהן and calls himself 'your lord'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מלך comes before a כהן גדול, as it says: 'And the king said to them: Take with you the servants of your lord.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues down the list and ranks the מלך above the כהן גדול, bringing a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, דוד המלך is speaking to צדוק the כהן, among others. He calls himself 'your lord'. That shows the king stands above the כהן.

phrases.english: A king comes before a High Priest,
as it says:
'And the king said to them:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the round-bracket word; the square-bracket word matches the actual wording of the פסוק.

phrases.english: Take with you
the servants of your lord, etc.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:33. Some versions have the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording. דוד is calling himself 'your lord' while speaking to צדוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next rung of the ranking: from חכם over מלך to מלך over כהן גדול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מלך takes priority over a כהן גדול.

steps.title: The כהן גדול comes before the נביא
steps.stepSummary: A כהן גדול comes before a נביא, because the פסוק mentions צדוק the כהן before נתן the נביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן גדול comes before a נביא, as it says: 'And let צדוק the כהן and נתן the נביא anoint him there.' The פסוק put צדוק before נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ranks the כהן גדול above the נביא and proves it from the order of names in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from word order. The פסוק names צדוק first and נתן second, and that order shows who ranks higher.

phrases.english: A High Priest comes before a prophet,
as it says:
'And let him anoint him there,
Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:34.

phrases.english: It put Zadok before Nathan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next rung of the ranking: כהן גדול over נביא. The list of כהנים and Temple officials continues in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול takes priority over a נביא.

steps.title: A second פסוק: יהושע the כהן גדול and his colleagues
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a second proof: a פסוק addresses יהושע the כהן גדול first, and then his colleagues.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it also says: 'Hear now, יהושע the כהן גדול, you and your colleagues, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second פסוק to support the rule that the כהן גדול comes before the נביא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks to יהושע the כהן גדול first and mentions his colleagues only after him. This works as a proof only if those colleagues were נביאים, and the next steps deal with that point.

keyTerms.meaning: And it also says (introduces an extra proof פסוק)

phrases.english: And it says:
'Hear now, Joshua the High Priest,
you and your colleagues, etc.'
phrases.notes: זכריה 3:8.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר: שְׁמַע נָא יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source for the same rule from step 26.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a כהן גדול comes before a נביא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: זכריה 3:8, where יהושע the כהן גדול is addressed before his colleagues.

steps.title: Maybe the colleagues were ordinary people
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a possible weak point: perhaps יהושע's colleagues were ordinary people, so the פסוק would prove nothing about נביאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think they were ordinary people.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pauses to raise a possible problem with its own proof, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the colleagues were ordinary people, then naming יהושע first is obvious and says nothing about how a כהן גדול ranks against a נביא. The proof would fall apart.

phrases.english: You might think they were ordinary people?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the proof in step 27 really works.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the colleagues were ordinary people, the פסוק shows nothing about a כהן גדול versus a נביא.

steps.title: 'Men of a sign' means prophets
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק calls the colleagues 'men of a sign' (מופת), and מופת always refers to a נביא, as the פסוק in דברים shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'For they are men of a sign.' And 'sign' means only a prophet, as it says: 'And he gives you a sign or a wonder.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the problem by showing that the colleagues were נביאים, so the proof from step 27 stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מופת is tied to prophecy, since in דברים a נביא is the one who gives an אות or a מופת. So 'men of a sign' means נביאים. Because יהושע the כהן גדול is named before these נביאים, the כהן גדול ranks higher.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign or wonder, linked to a prophet

steps.whatToRemember: The full ranking is: חכם, then מלך, then כהן גדול, then נביא. The last rung is proven both from the order צדוק before נתן and from יהושע being addressed before his נביא colleagues.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
'For they are men of a sign,'
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק, זכריה 3:8.

phrases.english: and 'sign' means nothing other than a prophet,
as it says:
'And he gives you a sign or a wonder.'
phrases.notes: דברים 13:2. That פסוק is about a נביא.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: כִּי אַנְשֵׁי מוֹפֵת הֵמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from step 28 and confirms the proof from step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying a word in the פסוק by comparing it to another פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The colleagues might have been ordinary people, so the פסוק would prove nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: מופת means נביא, so the colleagues were נביאים and the כהן גדול was named before them.

steps.title: Ranking the different kinds of כהן גדול down to the סגן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ranks a כהן גדול anointed with oil above one made by the garments, then former כהנים גדולים, then the משוח מלחמה, then the סגן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן גדול anointed with the anointing oil comes before a כהן גדול made by wearing the special garments. The garments one comes before a former anointed כהן גדול who stepped down because of קרי. That one comes before one who stepped down because of a blemish. That one comes before the משוח מלחמה. The משוח מלחמה comes before the סגן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of who gets honor first. Here it ranks the different kinds of כהן גדול and the כהנים just below them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person on the list comes before the next one. A current כהן גדול outranks a former one. Among former ones, the man who stepped down because of קרי, which is temporary, outranks the man who stepped down because of a lasting מום.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy anointing oil used to appoint a כהן גדול
A כהן גדול made so by wearing the special garments rather than by oil
A seminal emission, which makes a person טמא
A physical blemish that disqualifies a כהן from serving
The כהן anointed to speak to the army before war
The deputy of the כהן גדול, who replaces him if needed

phrases.english: One anointed with the anointing oil
precedes one with the multiple garments.
phrases.notes: Both are a כהן גדול. The second one became כהן גדול by putting on the special garments, not through the oil.

phrases.english: One with the multiple garments precedes
an anointed one who stepped down because of his seminal emission.
An anointed one who stepped down because of his seminal emission
precedes one who stepped down because of his blemish.
One who stepped down because of his blemish
precedes the one anointed for war.
The one anointed for war precedes the deputy.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשׁוּחַ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה קוֹדֵם לִמְרוּבֵּה בְגָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ranking that began with מלך, כהן גדול and נביא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Order: oil-anointed כהן גדול, then garments כהן גדול, then the one who stepped down for קרי, then the one who stepped down for a מום, then משוח מלחמה, then סגן.
steps.whyThisMatters: The line 'משוח מלחמה precedes סגן' is the exact line the גמרא will use for its challenge in step 37.

steps.title: The סגן comes before the אמרכל
steps.stepSummary: The ranking continues: the סגן comes before the אמרכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The סגן comes before the אמרכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The list moves one step further down and names a Temple official called the אמרכל. This also sets up the גמרא's next question about what that word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the list leaves the high כהונה positions and turns to the officials who ran the בית המקדש. The word אמרכל is unusual, so the גמרא stops to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: A senior official who oversaw the running of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: The deputy precedes the amarkal (overseer).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list directly from the סגן.

steps.title: What does the word אמרכל mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to ask what the word אמרכל means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is an אמרכל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the list to ask what this strange word means. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple question about a word, not a challenge. The גמרא wants to know who this official is before the list goes on.

phrases.english: What is "amarkal"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word that appeared in the previous line.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the title אמרכל.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the אמרכל is the one who 'says it all'
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that אמרכל means 'אמר כולא', the one who says everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it means 'he says it all.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by splitting the word into two parts: אמר כולא, 'he says all.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name describes the job. The אמרכל is the official whose word decides matters in running the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He says it all', the one who has the final word

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
"He says it all."
phrases.notes: He reads אמרכל as two words joined together: אמר (says) and כל (everything).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the word question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אמרכל is a joined form of אמר כולא, the official who has the final say.

steps.title: The rest of the list down to the ordinary כהן
steps.stepSummary: The list ends: אמרכל, then גזבר, then ראש משמר, then ראש בית אב, then כהן הדיוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The אמרכל comes before the גזבר. The גזבר comes before the ראש משמר. The ראש משמר comes before the ראש בית אב. The ראש בית אב comes before an ordinary כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes back to its list and finishes it, ending with the ordinary כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order goes from bigger responsibility to smaller. The ראש משמר leads a whole weekly group of כהנים, while a ראש בית אב leads only one family within that group, so he ranks lower.

keyTerms.meaning: The treasurer of the בית המקדש
Head of the weekly group of כהנים serving in the בית המקדש
Head of one family within a משמר, which served one day of the week
An ordinary כהן with no special position

steps.whatToRemember: Full order: חכם, מלך, כהן גדול, נביא. Then, among the כהנים: the oil-anointed כהן גדול, the מרובה בגדים, the one who stepped down for קרי, the one who stepped down for a מום, משוח מלחמה, סגן, אמרכל, גזבר, ראש משמר, ראש בית אב, כהן הדיוט.

phrases.english: The amarkal precedes the treasurer,
the treasurer precedes the head of the watch,

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁ מִשְׁמָר קוֹדֵם לְרֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב,
phrases.english: the head of the watch precedes the head of the family,

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב קוֹדֵם לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט.
phrases.english: the head of the family precedes an ordinary priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list after the word explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אמרכל, then גזבר, then ראש משמר, then ראש בית אב, then כהן הדיוט.

steps.title: For טומאה, which goes first: the סגן or the משוח מלחמה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the סגן and the משוח מלחמה should be the one to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: when it comes to becoming טמא, which goes first, the סגן or the משוח מלחמה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. When one of these two כהנים has to become טמא, which one should it be?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list told us who gets honor first. Now the גמרא asks a different question: who should 'go first' in becoming טמא? The honor ranking does not answer this by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים
With regard to becoming ritually impure

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
With regard to ritual impurity,
the deputy and the one anointed for war,
which of them precedes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses two people from the list to ask a new question about טומאה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the סגן or the משוח מלחמה should become טמא first when one of them must.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: the משוח מלחמה becomes טמא so the סגן stays ready
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the משוח מלחמה should become טמא for a מת מצוה, so the סגן stays טהור to replace the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב נחמן said: Come and hear a ברייתא. If a סגן and a משוח מלחמה were walking and found a מת מצוה, it is better that the משוח מלחמה become טמא and not the סגן. If something disqualifies the כהן גדול, the סגן goes in and serves in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא answers the question with a ברייתא. The משוח מלחמה should become טמא, not the סגן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is practical. The סגן is the backup for the כהן גדול, so he must stay טהור in case he is suddenly needed for the עבודה. The משוח מלחמה has no such backup job.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead body with no one else to bury it, which even a כהן must bury

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Nachman, said:
Come and hear, as it is taught:
A deputy and one anointed for war
who were walking along the road
and came upon a met מצוה,
it is better that the one anointed for war become impure
and the deputy not become impure,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם יֶאֱרַע בּוֹ פְּסוּל בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: for if a disqualification happens to the High Priest,
the deputy enters and serves in his place.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּתַנְיָא סְגָן וּמְשׁוּחַ מִלְחָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משוח מלחמה becomes טמא, so the סגן stays טהור as the backup for the כהן גדול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the two כהנים finding a מת מצוה on the road.

steps.title: But the list says the משוח מלחמה ranks higher than the סגן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the ברייתא's list puts the משוח מלחמה above the סגן, so how can he be the one to become טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: the משוח מלחמה comes before the סגן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a contradiction. The list said the משוח מלחמה is more important, yet here he is treated as the less important one who becomes טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משוח מלחמה ranks higher, we would expect to protect him and let the lower-ranked סגן become טמא. The new ברייתא seems to say the opposite.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second ברייתא is a different list. It is the same line we saw in step 30, 'משוח מלחמה קודם לסגן.'

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
The one anointed for war precedes the deputy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 36 using the list from step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the משוח מלחמה should become טמא and not the סגן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The higher-ranked person should be protected, and the list ranks the משוח מלחמה higher.

steps.title: רבינא: the list is about saving a life
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the list's ranking is about who gets saved first, not about who becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: that ברייתא was taught about saving his life.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא resolves the contradiction. The two ברייתות are talking about different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When it comes to saving a life, the משוח מלחמה comes first because he has higher standing. When it comes to טומאה, the סגן is protected because of his backup role for the עבודה. Each ruling has its own reason.

keyTerms.meaning: To keep him alive, meaning who gets rescued first

steps.whatToRemember: Honor and rescue go by rank, so the משוח מלחמה comes first. Staying טהור goes by the needs of the עבודה, so the סגן is protected.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that 'who comes first' can depend on the subject. Ranking for honor or rescue does not decide who must stay טהור.

phrases.english: Ravina said,
when that one was taught,
it was with regard to keeping him alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא לְהַחְיוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by limiting what the list is about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two subjects: the list is about saving a life, the other ברייתא is about טומאה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list's ranking applies to every situation, including טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list applies to saving a life. For טומאה the סגן is protected because he may need to replace the כהן גדול.

steps.title: The משנה's ranking list from כהן down to freed slave
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists who has priority: כהן, לוי, ישראל, ממזר, נתין, גר, עבד משוחרר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A כהן comes before a לוי. A לוי comes before a ישראל. A ישראל comes before a ממזר. A ממזר comes before a נתין. A נתין comes before a גר. A גר comes before a freed slave.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a ranking of seven kinds of people by family status, showing who gets priority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person on the list comes before everyone listed after him. Earlier, the גמרא was ranking positions inside the כהונה. Now the ranking is about family lineage across all of כלל ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden relationship (incest or adultery)
A descendant of the גבעונים, who joined the Jewish people in the days of יהושע
A freed non-Jewish slave, who becomes Jewish when he is freed

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A kohen comes before a levi,
a levi before a yisrael, a yisrael before a mamzer,
and a mamzer before a nasin, and a nasin before a convert,
and a convert before a freed slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of rankings within the כהונה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Priority goes in this order: כהן, לוי, ישראל, ממזר, נתין, גר, עבד משוחרר.

steps.title: Torah wisdom outranks family status
steps.stepSummary: The ranking only applies when people are equal in wisdom. A ממזר who is a תלמיד חכם comes before a כהן גדול who is an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? When they are all equal. But if a ממזר is a Torah scholar and a כהן גדול is ignorant, the scholar ממזר comes before the ignorant כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits its own list. Family status only decides things when the people are equal in Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה takes the most extreme case it can: the lowest-status person who is learned against the highest-status person who is ignorant. Even then, Torah learning wins. This shows Torah wisdom beats any family status.

keyTerms.meaning: An ignorant person, unlearned in Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Family status only breaks a tie. Torah learning comes first, even before a כהן גדול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic principle about honor in Judaism: Torah knowledge outranks lineage.

phrases.english: When? When they are all equal.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה מַמְזֵר תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
phrases.english: But if there was a mamzer who is a Torah scholar
and a kohen gadol who is ignorant —
the mamzer who is a Torah scholar comes before
the kohen gadol who is ignorant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the list from step 39 to cases of equal wisdom
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lineage ranking applies only when people are equal in wisdom. A learned ממזר comes before an ignorant כהן גדול.

steps.title: Verses showing כהן before לוי and לוי before ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק showing אהרן was set apart, so a כהן comes before a לוי. It brings another פסוק showing שבט לוי was set apart, so a לוי comes before a ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A כהן comes before a לוי, as it says: 'The sons of עמרם: אהרן and משה, and אהרן was set apart to be sanctified as most holy.' A לוי comes before a ישראל, as it says: 'At that time ה׳ set apart the tribe of לוי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the משנה's list. It gives a פסוק for each of the first two links.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה and אהרן were both לויים, yet only אהרן was 'set apart' for holiness. That shows a כהן is above a regular לוי. Then the whole tribe of לוי was 'set apart' from the other tribes, which shows a לוי is above a ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: GEMARA: A kohen comes before a levi —
as it says: 'The sons of Amram: Aharon and Moshe,'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 23:13. The words in round brackets are in the printed גמרא; the words in square brackets match the actual פסוק.

phrases.english: 'and Aharon was set apart to sanctify him as most holy.'
A levi comes before a yisrael —
as it says: 'At that time ה׳ set apart'
phrases.notes: דברים 10:8

phrases.english: 'the tribe of Levi,' and so on.
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in some printings but not in the פסוק itself. 'וגו׳' means the פסוק continues.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives פסוקים as sources for the first two links of the משנה's list
steps.raayaObject: The priority of כהן over לוי and of לוי over ישראל
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א 23:13 and דברים 10:8, which use the language of being 'set apart'

steps.title: Reasons for the rest of the ranking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a logical reason for each of the remaining links: lineage, Jewish parentage, growing up among the Jewish people, and the curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ישראל comes before a ממזר, because one has proper lineage and the other does not. A ממזר comes before a נתין, because one comes from Jewish parents and the other from non-Jewish parents. A נתין comes before a גר, because one grew up with us in holiness and the other did not. A גר comes before a freed slave, because the slave was under the curse and the גר was not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list. Instead of פסוקים, it gives a reason for each step down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each reason points to one specific thing the higher person has and the lower person lacks. A ממזר is still from Jewish parents, even though the union was forbidden. A נתין's family has lived as Jews for generations. The freed slave was once included in the curse of slavery, and the גר never was.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'a fit drop': born from Jewish parents
In holiness, living as part of the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: In the last reason the order flips. 'This one' (זה) was under the curse means the freed slave, and 'that one' was not means the גר.

phrases.english: A yisrael comes before a mamzer —
because this one has proper lineage, and that one does not have proper lineage.
A mamzer comes before a nasin —
this one comes from a fit drop,
phrases.notes: Meaning he was born from Jewish parents, even though the relationship was forbidden.

phrases.english: and that one comes from an unfit drop.
A nasin comes before a convert —
this one grew up with us in holiness,
and that one did not grow up with us in holiness.
A convert comes before a freed slave —
this one was included in the curse,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the freed slave here. The curse is the one placed on כנען, which covered Canaanite slaves.

phrases.english: and that one was not included in the curse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues down the list, giving reasons instead of פסוקים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each step down is explained by lineage, Jewish parentage, upbringing among the Jewish people, or the curse of slavery.

steps.title: Asking for the source that wisdom outranks lineage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's limit and asks where we learn it from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'When? When they are all equal,' and so on. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the second part of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the next step, where a פסוק is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a learned ממזר ahead of a כהן גדול is a big claim. The גמרא wants to know what in the תורה supports it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (asks for a source)
Etc.: the rest of the quote continues

phrases.english: 'When? When they are all equal,' and so on.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the list, returns to the משנה's limit and asks for its source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for the rule that a learned ממזר comes before an ignorant כהן גדול

steps.title: Torah is more precious than the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא ברבי חנינא brings the פסוק 'יקרה היא מפנינים' and reads it as: Torah is more precious than the כהן גדול who enters the inner sanctum.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא ברבי חנינא said: The פסוק says, 'She is more precious than pearls (פנינים).' This means more precious than the כהן גדול, who goes into the innermost place (לפני ולפנים).
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא ברבי חנינא answers the question with a פסוק about Torah, read as a play on words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word פנינים (pearls) sounds like לפני ולפנים, the innermost room, the קודש הקדשים, where only the כהן גדול may enter. So the פסוק says Torah is worth more than even the כהן גדול. That is why a learned ממזר comes before an ignorant כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: She (the Torah) is more precious than pearls
The innermost place: the קודש הקדשים

steps.whatToRemember: פנינים is read as לפני ולפנים, so Torah is more precious than the כהן גדול. This is the source that wisdom outranks lineage.

phrases.english: Rav Acha the son of Rabbi Chanina said:
as the verse says: 'She is more precious than pearls,'
phrases.notes: משלי 3:15. 'She' is the Torah's wisdom.

phrases.english: more than the kohen gadol who enters the innermost place.
phrases.notes: A play on words: מפנינים sounds like לפני ולפנים, the innermost holy room.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 43
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'יקרה היא מפנינים' shows Torah is more precious than the כהן גדול who enters לפני ולפנים.

steps.title: A גר comes before an עבד משוחרר because of the curse
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בר יוחאי admits a freed slave has a point in his favor, but the curse decides the order in favor of the convert.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בר יוחאי says: by logic, a freed slave should come before a convert, because the freed slave grew up among us in holiness and the convert did not. But the convert still comes first, because the slave was once under the curse and the convert never was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the earlier point that a גר comes before an עבד משוחרר because of the curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בר יוחאי first gives the freed slave a real advantage: he lived in a Jewish home and kept מצוות before he was freed. He then says the curse outweighs that advantage, so the גר still comes first. This supports the reason the גמרא gave in step 42.

keyTerms.meaning: Included in the curse given to כנען

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the first half as the final rule. רבי שמעון בר יוחאי only says what logic would suggest, and then he overturns it with 'אלא'. In the end, the convert comes first.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says:

phrases.aramaic: בַּדִּין הוּא שֶׁיַּקְדִּים עֶבֶד מְשׁוּחְרָר לְגֵר,
phrases.english: By right, a freed slave should come before a convert,
because this one (the slave) grew up with us in holiness,
and that one (the convert) did not grow up with us in holiness.
But this one (the slave) was included in the curse,
phrases.notes: This is the curse on כנען, 'ארור כנען' (בראשית 9:25).

phrases.english: and that one (the convert) was not included in the curse.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the convert-before-freed-slave link from step 42 and supports it with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a גר comes before an עבד משוחרר because of the curse.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בר יוחאי.

steps.title: Why do people prefer to marry a convert over a freed maidservant?
steps.stepSummary: The students of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק ask why a female convert is a more popular match than a freed maidservant.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students asked רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק: why is everyone eager to marry a female convert, but not everyone is eager to marry a freed maidservant?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related question about the same two groups, this time about marriage. This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same comparison as before, the convert against the freed slave, applied to women and marriage. The students noticed that people prefer one over the other and want to know why.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק:
phrases.english: His students asked Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה הַכֹּל רָצִין לִישָּׂא גִּיּוֹרֶת,
phrases.english: For what reason does everyone run to marry a female convert,
but not everyone runs to marry a freed maidservant?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the same comparison from step 45 into the area of marriage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason people prefer a female convert to a freed maidservant as a wife.

steps.title: Two reasons: the curse, and a presumption of modesty
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers with the curse. He then gives a second reason: the convert is presumed to have been guarded, and the maidservant is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told them: the maidservant was included in the curse, and the convert was not. Another answer: the convert is presumed to have been guarded, and the maidservant is not presumed to have been guarded.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives two separate reasons why people prefer to marry a convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is the same curse of כנען from step 45. The second reason is about behavior. A convert is presumed to have lived modestly. A maidservant, who lived without such protection, does not have that presumption.

keyTerms.meaning: Presumed to have been guarded, meaning she kept herself modest

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that 'זו' (this one) refers to a different woman in each answer. In the first answer it means the maidservant. In the second answer it means the convert.
steps.whatToRemember: People prefer to marry a convert over a freed maidservant for two reasons: the maidservant was once under the curse of כנען, and she does not have a presumption of modesty, while the convert does.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: זוֹ הָיְתָה בִּכְלַל אָרוּר,
phrases.english: He said to them: This one (the maidservant) was included in the curse,
and that one (the convert) was not included in the curse.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: זוֹ הָיְתָה בְּחֶזְקַת שָׁמוּר,
phrases.english: Another answer: this one (the convert) is presumed to have been guarded,
phrases.notes: Careful: here 'this one' switches to the convert.

phrases.english: and that one (the maidservant) is not presumed to have been guarded.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: זוֹ הָיְתָה בִּכְלַל אָרוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 46.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First, the curse of כנען. Second, the convert has a presumption of modesty and the maidservant does not.

steps.title: Why does a dog know its owner but a cat does not?
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רבי אלעזר why a dog recognizes its owner while a cat does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students asked רבי אלעזר: why does a dog recognize its owner, but a cat does not recognize its owner?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask another question, this time about animals. This step sets up רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic moves from people to animals. The students observed that dogs stay loyal and cats do not, and they want the reason.

phrases.english: His students asked Rabbi Elazar:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה הַכֶּלֶב מַכִּיר אֶת קוֹנוֹ,
phrases.english: For what reason does a dog recognize its owner,
while a cat does not recognize its owner?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another question the students asked, now about animals.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a cat does not recognize its owner the way a dog does.

steps.title: The cat eats the mouse itself, so it forgets
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers with a קל וחומר. Eating what a mouse ate makes a person forget, so eating the mouse itself certainly causes forgetting.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told them: if a person who eats from food a mouse ate becomes forgetful, then a cat, which eats the mouse itself, certainly becomes forgetful.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains that the cat forgets its owner because it eats mice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He starts from an accepted fact: eating food a mouse has eaten from causes forgetting. From there he argues a קל וחומר. If only the mouse's leftovers cause forgetting, eating the whole mouse must cause it even more. That is why the cat cannot remember its owner.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (the ending of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: He said to them: If one who eats
from what a mouse eats becomes forgetful,
then one who eats the mouse itself,
all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: וּמָה הָאוֹכֵל מִמַּה שֶּׁעַכְבָּר אוֹכֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 48.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר: the cat eats the mouse itself, so it forgets.

steps.title: Why do all animals prey on mice?
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רבי אליעזר why every animal overpowers mice.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students asked רבי אליעזר: why does everything overpower mice?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask one more question about mice. This step sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the last answer was about mice, the גמרא continues with another question about them. The students want to know why mice seem to be prey for every other animal.

phrases.english: His students asked Rabbi Eliezer:
For what reason does everything overpower mice?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of mice from step 49.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why mice are preyed on by everything.

steps.title: Because mice have a bad nature
steps.stepSummary: The answer: mice have a bad nature.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because their nature is bad.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers that mice are attacked by everything because their nature is bad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a creature with a bad nature deserves to be overpowered by others. What exactly is bad about their nature is explained in the next steps.

phrases.english: Because their nature is bad.

steps.title: What shows that mice have a bad nature?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the bad nature of mice actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an example of the mice's bad nature. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'their nature is bad' is too general. The גמרא wants a concrete sign of it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking for an explanation)

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of the answer in step 51.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete example of the mice's bad nature.

steps.title: Mice chew even clothing they cannot eat
steps.stepSummary: רבא says mice gnaw even cloaks, which they gain nothing from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: they gnaw even at cloaks.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the example: mice chew up even cloaks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cloak gives a mouse no food, so chewing it is pure damage. That is the proof of their bad nature: they destroy even when they get nothing out of it.
steps.whatToRemember: Mice are overpowered by everything because their nature is bad. The proof is that they destroy even cloaks, which give them no benefit.

phrases.english: Rava said: They gnaw even at cloaks.
